elements.element: Cap is mutual (applies to each Party)
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed"

elements.element: Cap limb (a): fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim" — anchored to the event, not to the claim

elements.element: Cap is the greater of limb (a) and limb (b)
elements.evidence: "shall not exceed the greater of (i) ... and (ii)"
"Neither Party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages or lost profits."

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: breach of confidentiality obligations
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality ... obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "The Company's obligations to make payments due under this Agreement ... shall not be treated as damages subject to this limitation."
"the greater of (i) the fees ... twelve (12) months ... and (ii) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000)" — a greater-of cap, not a cap of 12 months' fees

reasons: Preferred fee limb is anchored to "the event giving rise to the claim" rather than the 12 months preceding the claim; change to "in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" to match the locked preferred wording.
The fallback level is a separate bargain and is not satisfied either: a greater-of cap exceeds the fallback "cap of 12 months' fees", so the insertion cannot be scored down to the fallback.

The parenthetical "(including any Termination Payment)" introduces an undefined capitalised term into the Agreement, creating a dangling mechanic; it is also more than is needed since "payments due under this Agreement" already covers all amounts.
All other preferred elements (mutuality, USD 1,000,000 floor, mutual consequential-damages waiver, the full carve-out list, and the payment-obligations exclusion) are expressly present.
